papers.title: Attention regulation and monitoring in meditation
papers.summary: Introduces the focused-attention versus open-monitoring distinction that most later studies use to classify meditation styles, and links each to attention networks.

papers.title: Reconstructing and deconstructing the self: cognitive mechanisms in meditation practice
papers.summary: Proposes three families of practice (attentional, constructive, deconstructive) organised around how they change self-related processing.

papers.title: The plasticity of well-being: A training-based framework for the cultivation of human flourishing
papers.summary: Frames well-being as trainable skills (awareness, connection, insight, purpose) and maps each onto candidate neural and psychological mechanisms.

papers.title: The neuroscience of mindfulness meditation
papers.summary: Widely cited overview of attention control, emotion regulation and self-awareness as the three components through which mindfulness is thought to act on the brain.

papers.title: How does mindfulness meditation work? Proposing mechanisms of action from a conceptual and neural perspective
papers.summary: Breaks mindfulness into interacting mechanisms (attention regulation, body awareness, emotion regulation, change in self-perspective) with proposed neural substrates.

papers.title: Investigating the phenomenological matrix of mindfulness-related practices from a neurocognitive perspective
papers.summary: Describes practices as positions in a multidimensional space (object orientation, meta-awareness, dereification and others) instead of discrete categories.

papers.title: From many to (n)one: Meditation and the plasticity of the predictive mind
papers.summary: Recasts meditation within predictive processing: practice progressively flattens the predictive hierarchy, with cessation as the limit case.

papers.title: Towards a computational phenomenology of mental action: modelling meta-awareness and attentional control with deep parametric active inference
papers.summary: Builds a hierarchical active-inference model in which meta-awareness controls attentional precision, and simulates mind-wandering and its correction during breath focus.

papers.title: Mind the hype: A critical evaluation and prescriptive agenda for research on mindfulness and meditation
papers.summary: Critiques weak definitions, small samples and overstated claims in mindfulness research, and sets out a methodological agenda for the field.

papers.title: Long-term meditators self-induce high-amplitude gamma synchrony during mental practice
papers.summary: Tibetan Buddhist practitioners generating non-referential compassion showed unusually large gamma-band power and synchrony compared with novices.

papers.title: Meditation states and traits: EEG, ERP, and neuroimaging studies
papers.summary: Classic review separating short-term state effects from long-term trait effects, with alpha and theta changes as the most consistent EEG findings at the time.

papers.title: Occipital gamma activation during Vipassana meditation
papers.summary: Long-term Vipassana practitioners showed increased occipital gamma power during meditation relative to a control thinking state.

papers.title: A systematic review of the neurophysiology of mindfulness on EEG oscillations
papers.summary: Systematic review of EEG oscillation studies; increased alpha and theta are the most consistent findings, while gamma and beta results are mixed.

papers.title: Increased Gamma Brainwave Amplitude Compared to Control in Three Different Meditation Traditions
papers.summary: Compared Vipassana, Himalayan Yoga and Isha Shoonya practitioners with controls and found higher parieto-occipital gamma across traditions.

papers.title: Reduced mind wandering in experienced meditators and associated EEG correlates
papers.summary: Experience-sampling probes during meditation showed experts reported less mind wandering; frontal midline theta and somatosensory alpha were higher during meditation than during wandering. The data are openly shared (see datasets).

papers.title: Experienced mindfulness meditators exhibit higher parietal-occipital EEG gamma activity during NREM sleep
papers.summary: Long-term practitioners showed elevated parieto-occipital gamma during NREM sleep, suggesting a trait effect that persists outside practice.

papers.title: Mindfulness-induced changes in gamma band activity – implications for the default mode network, self-reference and attention
papers.summary: Relates practice-related gamma changes in experienced mindfulness meditators to reduced default-mode, self-referential activity.

papers.title: Mindfulness starts with the body: somatosensory attention and top-down modulation of cortical alpha rhythms in mindfulness meditation
papers.summary: Proposes that early mindfulness training works by sharpening top-down control of somatosensory alpha rhythms during body-focused attention.

papers.title: Nonlinear EEG signatures of mind wandering during breath focus meditation
papers.summary: Tests whether nonlinear (complexity) EEG measures distinguish mind wandering from breath focus in novice meditators.

papers.title: Oscillating Mindfully: Using Machine Learning to Characterize Systems-Level Electrophysiological Activity During Focused Attention Meditation
papers.summary: Gradient-boosted classifiers with feature-importance analysis separated focused attention from mind wandering in 26 experienced meditators, highlighting high-frequency power and coherence features.

papers.title: Using Electroencephalography to Advance Mindfulness Science: A Survey of Emerging Methods and Approaches
papers.authors: Lin Y, Atad DA, Zanesco AP
papers.venue: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging
papers.summary: Survey of newer EEG analyses for mindfulness research, including separating oscillatory from aperiodic activity and complexity measures, with notes on their caveats.

papers.title: Neural correlates of attentional expertise in long-term meditation practitioners
papers.summary: Concentration meditation engaged attention networks in an inverted-U relation with practice hours: moderate experts showed more activation than novices, the most practised showed less.

papers.title: Meditation experience is associated with differences in default mode network activity and connectivity
papers.summary: Experienced meditators showed lower activity in core default-mode regions across several practices, and stronger coupling between posterior cingulate and control regions.

papers.title: Mind wandering and attention during focused meditation: A fine-grained temporal analysis of fluctuating cognitive states
papers.summary: Participants pressed a button when they noticed mind wandering, revealing a cycle of wandering, awareness, shifting and sustained attention with distinct network activity.

papers.title: Meditation leads to reduced default mode network activity beyond an active task
papers.summary: Compared with an active cognitive task baseline, meditation still reduced activity in default-mode regions such as posterior cingulate cortex.

papers.title: Attending to the present: mindfulness meditation reveals distinct neural modes of self-reference
papers.summary: After mindfulness training, experiential (moment-to-moment) self-focus shifted activity away from medial prefrontal narrative regions toward lateral and insular regions.

papers.title: Regulation of the neural circuitry of emotion by compassion meditation: effects of meditative expertise
papers.summary: During compassion meditation, experts showed stronger insula and cingulate responses to emotional vocal sounds than novices.

papers.title: Compassion training alters altruism and neural responses to suffering
papers.summary: Two weeks of compassion training increased altruistic redistribution in an economic game, and this was linked to changed responses to images of suffering.

papers.title: Differential pattern of functional brain plasticity after compassion and empathy training
papers.summary: Empathy training increased negative affect and related activity, while subsequent compassion training raised positive affect and engaged reward-related regions.

papers.title: Focus on the breath: Brain decoding reveals internal states of attention during meditation
papers.summary: Trained brain-pattern classifiers on attention tasks and applied them to meditation to estimate moment-to-moment breath focus versus mind wandering.

papers.title: Meditation experience is associated with increased cortical thickness
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study reporting thicker prefrontal and insular cortex in experienced insight meditators. Small sample; later work urges caution.

papers.title: Mindfulness practice leads to increases in regional brain gray matter density
papers.summary: Early longitudinal MBSR study reporting gray-matter density increases. Not reproduced in the much larger trial by Kral et al. (2022).

papers.title: Is meditation associated with altered brain structure? A systematic review and meta-analysis of morphometric neuroimaging in meditation practitioners
papers.summary: Meta-analysis of structural studies finding modest, regionally consistent differences, alongside a warning about publication bias and small samples.

papers.title: Functional neuroanatomy of meditation: A review and meta-analysis of 78 functional neuroimaging investigations
papers.summary: Coordinate-based meta-analysis showing that different practice families recruit partly distinct networks rather than a single "meditation" signature.

papers.title: Absence of structural brain changes from mindfulness-based stress reduction: Two combined randomized controlled trials
papers.summary: Pooled two randomized trials (n = 218) with active and waitlist controls and found no MBSR-specific change in gray-matter volume or cortical thickness after eight weeks.

papers.title: Structural plasticity of the social brain: Differential change after socio-affective and cognitive mental training
papers.summary: In the nine-month ReSource Project, each training module produced its own pattern of cortical thickness change, matched to behavioural gains.

papers.title: Specific reduction in cortisol stress reactivity after social but not attention-based mental training
papers.summary: In the ReSource Project, socio-affective and socio-cognitive (dyadic) modules lowered cortisol responses to a social stressor; attention-based training did not.

papers.title: ENIGMA-Meditation: Worldwide Consortium for Neuroscientific Investigations of Meditation Practices
papers.venue: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging
papers.summary: Launches an ENIGMA working group to pool meditation neuroimaging datasets worldwide with shared pipelines for meta- and mega-analysis.

papers.title: The functional neuroimaging of meditation: A quantitative whole-brain meta-analysis and systematic review
papers.summary: Preregistered whole-brain meta-analysis of 34 fMRI studies (about 700 people) comparing focused attention, open monitoring, mantra and loving-kindness practices.

papers.title: Short-term meditation training improves attention and self-regulation
papers.summary: Five days of integrative body-mind training improved executive attention and lowered cortisol responses relative to relaxation training.

papers.title: Mental training affects distribution of limited brain resources
papers.summary: A three-month Vipassana retreat reduced the attentional blink, with smaller P3b responses to the first target suggesting more efficient resource allocation.

papers.title: Alterations in brain and immune function produced by mindfulness meditation
papers.summary: Workplace MBSR increased left-sided frontal EEG activation and antibody response to a flu vaccine compared with a waitlist.

papers.title: Mindfulness training improves working memory capacity and GRE performance while reducing mind wandering
papers.summary: Two weeks of mindfulness training reduced mind wandering and improved working memory and reading comprehension scores versus a nutrition class.

papers.title: Meditation programs for psychological stress and well-being: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.summary: Mindfulness programs showed moderate evidence for reducing anxiety, depression and pain, with little evidence for mantra programs. Effects were comparable to other active treatments.

papers.title: Mindfulness-based interventions for psychiatric disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.summary: Mindfulness interventions outperformed no treatment and some active controls across psychiatric conditions, and matched evidence-based treatments.

papers.title: Mindfulness Meditation and Psychopathology
papers.summary: Reviews clinical evidence and candidate mechanisms for mindfulness in depression, anxiety, addiction and other conditions.

papers.title: Systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials assessing mindfulness-based programs for mental health promotion
papers.summary: Individual-participant meta-analysis of trials in non-clinical settings: small average benefits for distress, with little evidence that benefits differ by participant traits.

papers.title: Effects of Contemplative Dyads on Engagement and Perceived Social Connectedness Over 9 Months of Mental Training: A Randomized Clinical Trial
papers.summary: Partner-based contemplative dyads in the ReSource Project increased daily feelings of social connection compared with solitary practice.

papers.title: Brain mechanisms supporting the modulation of pain by mindfulness meditation
papers.summary: After four days of training, meditating reduced pain ratings, linked to activity in anterior cingulate, insula and orbitofrontal cortex.

papers.title: A non-elaborative mental stance and decoupling of executive and pain-related cortices predicts low pain sensitivity in Zen meditators
papers.summary: Zen practitioners showed lower pain sensitivity with reduced prefrontal engagement and decoupling between executive and pain-related regions.

papers.title: Altered anterior insula activation during anticipation and experience of painful stimuli in expert meditators
papers.summary: Expert practitioners in open presence rated pain as less unpleasant, with higher insula activity during pain and faster habituation in amygdala.

papers.title: Neural correlates of nondual awareness in meditation
papers.venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.summary: Reviews evidence that nondual awareness alters the usual anticorrelation between intrinsic (default) and extrinsic (task-positive) networks.

papers.title: Psychedelics, Meditation, and Self-Consciousness
papers.summary: Compares self-loss in meditation and psychedelic states, arguing both are tools for dissecting the components of self-consciousness.

papers.title: Investigation of advanced mindfulness meditation “cessation” experiences using EEG spectral analysis in an intensively sampled case study
papers.summary: Thirty-seven cessation events in one adept showed a large alpha-power decline beginning about 40 seconds before each event, lowest just after it.

papers.title: Neurophenomenological Investigation of Mindfulness Meditation “Cessation” Experiences Using EEG Network Analysis in an Intensively Sampled Adept Meditator
papers.summary: Network analysis of the same cessation recordings showing large-scale changes in functional connectivity around cessation events.

papers.title: Intensive whole-brain 7T MRI case study of volitional control of brain activity in deep absorptive meditation states
papers.summary: Twenty-seven 7T fMRI runs over five days in one adept during jhana revealed state-specific activity in cortex, thalamus, brainstem and cerebellum, related to rated jhana qualities.

papers.title: Multimodal neurophenomenology of advanced concentration absorption meditation: An intensively sampled case study of Jhana
papers.summary: Combined fMRI, EEG and experience ratings in one practitioner with over 23,000 hours; jhana states showed reduced network modularity and default–visual desegregation.

papers.title: Neuromodulation and meditation: A review and synthesis toward promoting well-being and understanding consciousness and brain
papers.summary: Reviews studies combining non-invasive brain stimulation with meditation and argues for using stimulation to test causal mechanisms, including of advanced states.

papers.title: A default mode of brain function
papers.summary: Defines the brain's resting "default mode", the network that meditation studies most often report as changed.

papers.title: Mind-wandering as spontaneous thought: a dynamic framework
papers.summary: Describes mind wandering as thought with weak deliberate and automatic constraints, a useful lens for what meditation trains.

papers.title: Parameterizing neural power spectra into periodic and aperiodic components
papers.summary: Introduces FOOOF (now specparam) for separating oscillatory peaks from the aperiodic 1/f component, important for re-reading older band-power meditation findings.

papers.title: MEG and EEG data analysis with MNE-Python
papers.summary: The reference paper for MNE-Python, the most widely used open EEG/MEG toolbox in Python.

papers.title: The brain imaging data structure, a format for organizing and describing outputs of neuroimaging experiments
papers.summary: Defines BIDS, the folder and metadata standard used by OpenNeuro and most open datasets listed here.

papers.title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
papers.summary: Extends BIDS to EEG so recordings can be shared and loaded with standard tools.

papers.title: The OpenNeuro resource for sharing of neuroscience data
papers.summary: Describes OpenNeuro, the main free archive for BIDS-formatted neuroimaging and electrophysiology data.

papers.title: Neurosynth Compose: A web-based platform for flexible and reproducible neuroimaging meta-analysis
papers.summary: Web platform for curated, reproducible coordinate-based meta-analyses, built on NeuroStore and executed with NiMARE.

papers.title: MNE-LSL: Real-time framework integrated with MNE-Python for online neuroscience research through LSL-compatible devices
papers.summary: Real-time streaming on top of MNE-Python via Lab Streaming Layer, useful for meditation neurofeedback.

papers.title: L-FAME: Longitudinal Focused Attention Meditation EEG Dataset and Benchmark
papers.summary: Pre/post EEG from 74 students across six weeks of breath-focus or mantra training, with benchmark tasks for state decoding, technique classification and cross-session transfer.

papers.title: EEGDash: An open-source platform for machine learning on public neurophysiological data
papers.summary: Registry and loader that streams public BIDS EEG/MEG datasets from OpenNeuro and NEMAR straight into PyTorch and braindecode.

papers.title: Large Brain Model for Learning Generic Representations with Tremendous EEG Data in BCI
papers.authors: Jiang WB, Zhao LM, Lu BL
papers.summary: A widely used EEG foundation model pretrained on large pooled EEG with channel-wise patches and a neural codebook.

papers.title: CBraMod: A Criss-Cross Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding
papers.summary: EEG foundation model with criss-cross spatial/temporal attention, evaluated on 10 downstream BCI tasks.

papers.title: EEG-FM-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for the Systematic Evaluation of EEG Foundation Models
papers.summary: Standardised benchmark comparing EEG foundation models (BENDR, BIOT, LaBraM, EEGPT, CBraMod, CSBrain, REVE).

papers.title: SciRepEval: A Multi-Format Benchmark for Scientific Document Representations
papers.summary: Introduces SPECTER2 and the SciRepEval benchmark for scientific paper embeddings; a strong baseline for the paper finder.

papers.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
papers.summary: The sentence-transformers approach behind MiniLM-style encoders used by the paper finder.

papers.title: Why is it so hard to do my work? The challenge of attention residue when switching between work tasks
papers.venue: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
papers.summary: Introduces attention residue: after switching away from a task, thoughts about it persist and hurt performance on the next task, especially when the first task was left unfinished. The origin of the concept.

papers.title: The effect of regulatory focus on attention residue and performance during interruptions
papers.venue: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
papers.summary: Tests whether a person's motivational orientation (promotion versus prevention focus) changes how much residue an interruption leaves and how well they perform afterwards.

papers.title: Tasks Interrupted: How Anticipating Time Pressure on Resumption of an Interrupted Task Causes Attention Residue and Low Performance on Interrupting Tasks and How a "Ready-to-Resume" Plan Mitigates the Effects
papers.summary: Four studies: expecting time pressure when returning to an interrupted task increases residue and lowers performance on the interrupting task. Briefly planning the return ("ready-to-resume") removes the effect, a simple intervention comparable to the disengage-and-return step trained in meditation.

papers.title: Interruptions and Task Transitions: Understanding Their Characteristics, Processes, and Consequences
papers.authors: Leroy S, Schmidt AM, Madjar N
papers.summary: Integrative review of research on interruptions and transitions between tasks, organising what is known about their types, the attentional and motivational processes they set off, and their consequences.

papers.title: Reset a task set after five minutes of mindfulness practice
papers.summary: A previous task's attentional settings carried over into a new visual search task after five minutes of scene viewing or distraction, but not after five minutes of mindfulness practice. The closest laboratory evidence that meditation clears residue from a prior task.

papers.title: Effects of Brief Mindfulness Meditation on Attention Switching
papers.summary: After an anxiety-inducing film, brief mindfulness training sped responses overall compared with worry or free mind-wandering, but did not reduce the switch cost itself. A useful null for claims that meditation specifically improves switching.

papers.title: Mindfulness as Attention Training: Meta-Analyses on the Links Between Attention Performance and Mindfulness Interventions, Long-Term Meditation Practice, and Trait Mindfulness
papers.summary: Separate meta-analyses relating attention task performance to mindfulness interventions, long-term practice and trait mindfulness; a starting point for judging which attention components, including switching, meditation actually changes.

papers.title: Meditation, Mindfulness, and Attention: a Meta-analysis
papers.summary: Meta-analysis of meditation and mindfulness effects across attention measures; read with Verhaeghen (2020) for the evidence on attentional control and disengagement.

papers.title: Neuropsychological aspects of digital distraction: a randomized controlled experimental study
papers.summary: Randomised experiment (n = 87) combining executive-function tasks, workload ratings and 7-channel EEG recorded via LSL under intermittent audiovisual distraction. Error rates barely changed; a template for measuring interruption costs neurally, not a meditation study.

datasets.name: BIDS formatted EEG meditation experiment data
datasets.description: 64-channel Biosemi EEG from expert and non-expert meditators, interrupted roughly every two minutes by probes rating concentration and mind wandering. Basis of Brandmeyer & Delorme (2018). About 9 GB, BIDS formatted. Also mirrored on OpenNeuro.

datasets.name: L-FAME: Longitudinal Focused Attention Meditation EEG
datasets.description: 64-channel EEG and questionnaires before and after six weeks of breath focus or one of two mantra practices, with benchmark tasks and code. Hosted on Hugging Face.

datasets.name: PsiConnect: multimodal neuroimaging under psilocybin with meditation training
datasets.description: Multi-echo fMRI and EEG at rest and during guided meditation, music and movie watching, before and after psilocybin; half the cohort did eight weeks of meditation training. Described as an openly curated, reusable dataset.
datasets.note: Check the PsiConnect data paper for the release location.

datasets.name: OpenNeuro: meditation datasets
datasets.description: Search OpenNeuro for "meditation" or "mindfulness" to find BIDS datasets; every upload passes BIDS validation, and most are CC0.

datasets.name: EEGDash catalog (OpenNeuro + NEMAR, 700+ datasets)
datasets.description: Not a meditation dataset itself: a registry that loads any public BIDS EEG dataset into PyTorch/braindecode with one call. Useful for pretraining or pooling resting-state data as controls.

datasets.name: ReSource Project (Max Planck)
datasets.description: Nine-month, three-module mental training study (Presence, Affect, Perspective) run 2012–2016 in Leipzig and Berlin. Data are not openly posted; publications are listed by the Social Neuroscience Lab and data access is by collaboration.

datasets.name: ENIGMA-Meditation consortium
datasets.description: Not a public download: a consortium pooling meditation neuroimaging datasets for harmonised mega-analysis. Labs with data can join.

datasets.name: NeuroStore (Neurosynth Compose)
datasets.description: 30,000+ studies with pre-extracted activation coordinates. Filter for meditation studies to run your own coordinate-based meta-analysis in Neurosynth Compose.

tools.name: MNE-Python
tools.description: Preprocessing, ICA, time-frequency, source imaging and statistics for M/EEG. The default starting point.

tools.name: specparam (formerly FOOOF)
tools.description: Splits power spectra into aperiodic (1/f) and periodic peaks. Version 2.0 is still a release candidate and adds time-resolved and event-related models. Re-test any "alpha/theta increase" claim with it.

tools.name: MNE-BIDS
tools.description: Read and write BIDS datasets from MNE; needed to load OpenNeuro data cleanly.

tools.name: EEGLAB
tools.description: Long-standing MATLAB toolbox (ICA, plugins, NEMAR integration), used by many meditation EEG studies.

tools.name: NeuroKit2
tools.description: Heart rate variability, respiration, EDA and ECG processing, for the physiology side of practice studies.

tools.name: fMRIPrep
tools.description: Robust, standardised fMRI preprocessing for BIDS data; the usual first step before harmonised analyses.

tools.name: Nilearn
tools.description: Connectivity, decoding and GLMs on fMRI in Python.

tools.name: NiMARE
tools.description: Coordinate- and image-based meta-analysis (ALE, MKDA and more); the engine behind Neurosynth Compose.

tools.name: Neurosynth Compose
tools.description: Curate studies, annotate them and run reproducible meta-analyses in the browser, backed by NeuroStore.

tools.name: Lab Streaming Layer (LSL)
tools.description: Time-synchronised streaming across devices; supported by most research EEG systems.

tools.name: MNE-LSL
tools.description: Real-time streams and buffers integrated with MNE-Python, for neurofeedback-guided meditation.

tools.name: BrainFlow
tools.description: One API for many consumer and research biosensors (OpenBCI, Muse and others).

tools.name: OpenBCI
tools.description: Open hardware boards (Cyton, Ganglion) and GUI; a low-cost route to running your own meditation EEG study.

tools.name: EEG-Notebooks
tools.description: Ready-made experiments for consumer EEG headsets, good for teaching and pilot data.

tools.name: braindecode
tools.description: Deep learning for EEG in PyTorch, with model zoo and dataset loaders.

tools.name: EEGDash
tools.description: Streams 700+ public BIDS datasets from OpenNeuro and NEMAR into PyTorch / braindecode.

tools.name: LaBraM
tools.description: EEG foundation model; fine-tune on small meditation datasets instead of training from scratch.

tools.name: CBraMod
tools.description: EEG foundation model with criss-cross attention; a strong recent baseline in benchmarks.

tools.name: EEG-FM-Bench
tools.description: Benchmark for comparing EEG foundation models on standard tasks before choosing one.

tools.name: sentence-transformers
tools.description: Training and inference for contrastive text encoders; used in clm/ to fine-tune and embed the corpus.

tools.name: Transformers.js
tools.description: Runs ONNX models in the browser (WASM or WebGPU); powers the on-device paper finder.

tools.name: SPECTER2
tools.description: Scientific paper embeddings trained on citation triplets; a heavier but stronger alternative encoder.

databases.name: Europe PMC
databases.notes: No key needed. resultType=core returns abstracts, MeSH terms and licence info. Used by the finder's live search and the corpus builder.

databases.name: OpenAlex
databases.coverage: 250M+ works, CC0 metadata and citation graph
databases.notes: Since 13 Feb 2026 the API needs a free key (about $1/day of free usage; keyless is a small demo quota). Abstracts come as an inverted index. Best for citation pairs. Bulk snapshot remains free on S3.

databases.name: Semantic Scholar API
databases.notes: Recommendations endpoint suggests recent papers from positive/negative seed papers. Low anonymous rate limits; request a key for heavy use.

databases.name: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities)
databases.notes: MeSH term "Meditation" is the cleanest filter. Optional key raises rate limits.

databases.name: arXiv
databases.notes: Metadata (including abstracts) is CC0, so it is safe to redistribute in the corpus.

databases.name: bioRxiv / medRxiv
databases.notes: Where many neuroimaging meditation papers appear first.

databases.name: OpenNeuro
databases.coverage: 1,000+ BIDS datasets: MRI, EEG, MEG, iEEG, PET
databases.notes: Every dataset passes BIDS validation; most are CC0.

databases.name: NEMAR
databases.coverage: OpenNeuro EEG/MEG with compute at SDSC
databases.notes: Run EEGLAB/MNE pipelines on OpenNeuro electrophysiology without downloading.

databases.name: DANDI Archive
databases.notes: Mainly animal and intracranial data; relevant for mechanistic work.

databases.name: Zenodo
databases.notes: Hosts several meditation EEG datasets, including the Delorme meditation set.

databases.name: Hugging Face Datasets
databases.coverage: ML-ready datasets, incl. EEGDash mirrors and L-FAME
databases.notes: Increasingly where EEG benchmarks are released.

databases.name: NeuroStore / Neurosynth
databases.notes: Basis for custom meta-analyses of meditation fMRI.

organizations.name: Center for Healthy Minds (UW–Madison)
organizations.focus: Well-being training, compassion, long-term practitioners, large RCTs

organizations.name: Meditation Research Program (MGH / Harvard Medical School)
Lutz team, Lyon Neuroscience Research Center (CRNL)
organizations.focus: Neurophenomenology, meta-awareness, active-inference models of meditation

organizations.name: Social Neuroscience Lab (Max Planck Society), Berlin
organizations.focus: ReSource Project, compassion and empathy training, contemplative dyads

organizations.name: Swartz Center for Computational Neuroscience (UCSD) / CerCo Toulouse
organizations.focus: EEGLAB, NEMAR, EEGDash, meditation EEG and open data

organizations.name: Mind & Life Institute
organizations.focus: Founded 1991. Summer Research Institute and research grants (Varela and others, up to $25,000) for early-career researchers who attended the Summer Research Institute.

organizations.name: BIAL Foundation
organizations.focus: Grants for psychophysiology, including several advanced-meditation studies

organizations.name: International Society for Contemplative Research (ISCR)
organizations.focus: Professional society and conference for contemplative science

organizations.name: NeuroTechX
organizations.focus: Neurotech community, hackathons, EEG-ExPy; useful for BCI-flavoured meditation projects

concepts.name: Focused attention (FA)
concepts.definition: Holding attention on one object (often the breath), noticing when it drifts and bringing it back. The cycle of wandering, noticing and returning is itself a common study target.

concepts.name: Open monitoring (OM)
concepts.definition: Non-selective awareness of whatever arises, without fixing on an object. Vipassana and many "open presence" practices fall here.

concepts.name: Compassion and loving-kindness
concepts.definition: Constructive practices that cultivate care for others' suffering or wishes for their well-being. Distinct in brain and behaviour from empathic distress.

concepts.name: Non-dual awareness
concepts.definition: Practices aiming at awareness without a felt split between observer and observed. Studied mostly in very experienced practitioners.

concepts.name: Mind wandering
concepts.definition: Thought that drifts away from the current task. Meditation studies use it both as the thing being trained and as a control state.

concepts.name: Default mode network (DMN)
concepts.definition: Medial prefrontal, posterior cingulate and parietal regions active during rest and self-related thought. Reduced DMN activity is one of the most reported meditation findings.

concepts.name: Neurophenomenology
concepts.definition: Pairing careful first-person reports with neural data so experience constrains the analysis. Proposed by Varela in 1996; now central to advanced-meditation research.

concepts.name: Advanced meditation (jhana, cessation)
concepts.definition: States and stages reported by highly experienced practitioners, such as the absorptions (jhanas) or cessation events where experience briefly stops. Usually studied with intensive sampling of one or a few adepts.

concepts.name: Predictive processing and active inference
concepts.definition: Frameworks in which the brain minimises prediction error. Meditation is modelled as changing the precision (confidence) given to predictions and sensations.

concepts.name: Aperiodic (1/f) EEG activity
concepts.definition: The broadband, non-oscillatory part of the power spectrum. Changes in it can masquerade as band-power changes, so newer analyses separate the two.

concepts.name: State versus trait effects
concepts.definition: State effects occur during practice; trait effects persist outside it, e.g. at rest or in sleep. Long-term-practitioner studies try to separate them.

concepts.name: Active control groups
concepts.definition: Comparison programmes matched for expectation and effort but without meditation (e.g. the Health Enhancement Program). Needed to attribute effects to meditation itself.

concepts.name: Attention residue
concepts.definition: Sophie Leroy's term for the part of attention that stays on a previous task after switching to a new one, lowering performance on the new task; it is larger when the first task is unfinished or will be resumed under time pressure. Cognitive psychology studies the same carryover as task-set inertia. Brief mindfulness practice may clear it, though evidence is still behavioural and there is little neuroimaging work yet.
